home.subtitle: Virtual Biophysics Engine
home.tagline1a: A deterministic biophysics simulator. You specify the cell pair and protocol, it solves Schwan, Pennes, and Lorentzian models to predict membrane voltage, disruption ratio, and the
home.tagline1b: : the frequency band where target cells cross the lysis threshold while healthy cells stay below. Every number comes with a visible equation and a peer-reviewed citation.
home.tagline2: Nine physics models, thirty-two references, two replicated benchmarks. Live impedance feedback, AI protocol optimizer, and publication-ready Methods export, all in one bench workspace.
home.wf1Desc: 20 built-in presets plus your own custom cell profiles. Any target-healthy pair, one click.
home.wf2Desc: Live Vm, disruption ratio, SAR, and DEP as you tune.
home.wf3Desc: AI optimizer. Selectivity window sweep. Publication export.
home.card1Desc: Live biophysics at every slider position.
home.card2Desc: Real impedance feedback and corrected generator voltage.
home.card3Desc: Publication-ready Methods export in one click.
home.card4Desc: 20 built-in presets plus custom profiles. Add any cell type from your own measurements to the shared lab library.

home.tipSciCell: Schwan equation: Vm = 1.5 E R cos(θ) / √(1+(ωτ)²). Cyan ions drift toward the +Vm pole, red toward -Vm, building the transmembrane potential that drives electroporation. Click to explore in the lab.
home.tipSciChart: Vm rolls off above the characteristic frequency fc = 1/(2πτ). Below fc the membrane fully charges; above fc it stays sub-threshold. The animated dot illustrates the roll-off behaviour. Click to open the Experiment Lab and tune parameters live.
